headline: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital
summary: A fault in the air conditioning system triggered a blaze at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, leaving only one infant rescued from the ward.
details: At least 15 infants were killed when a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's capital.
The blaze started around 7 a.m. on the third floor of the hospital's mother and child health ward.
According to local broadcaster Geo TV, the fire was triggered by a fault in the air conditioning systems.
There were 16 newborns in the ward at the time of the incident; only one was successfully rescued.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation to identify those responsible and ensure the strictest action is taken.
PIMS is one of the city's main public hospitals, though state-run facilities in Pakistan have faced frequent criticism for being under-resourced and mismanaged.
caption:
15 infants killed. Only one rescued.

A devastating fire at a state-run hospital in Islamabad has claimed the lives of 15 newborns.

At least 15 infants were killed when a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's capital.

The blaze started around 7 a.m. on the third floor of the hospital's mother and child health ward.

According to local broadcaster Geo TV, the fire was triggered by a fault in the air conditioning systems.

There were 16 newborns in the ward at the time of the incident; only one was successfully rescued.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation to identify those responsible and ensure the strictest action is taken.

PIMS is one of the city's main public hospitals, though state-run facilities in Pakistan have faced frequent criticism for being under-resourced and mismanaged.

headline_marked: Country music icon [[Dolly Parton dies at 80]] after cancer battle
headline: Country music icon Dolly Parton dies at 80 after cancer battle
summary: The legendary singer and actress leaves behind a massive legacy of hits like "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," prompting tributes from global stars.
details: Legendary country singer and actress Dolly Parton has passed away at the age of 80. According to a statement from her family, she died on August 25 after privately battling cancer.
Parton is globally recognized for her timeless hits such as "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," as well as her significant contributions to film and philanthropy.
Music and Hollywood stars have poured out their tributes. Reba McEntire praised Parton's "huge heart," while Lily Tomlin called her the "Great Harmonizer of Humanity."
Taylor Swift described the icon as a "gift that kept on giving," noting her influence on young women and her "backbone of steel" as an artist.
US President Donald Trump mourned the loss, calling her one of the greatest country singers and describing her death as a "true loss for millions of people."
Other tributes came from Jane Fonda, Sally Field, and Julia Roberts, who remembered her kindness, humor, and magical spirit.
Paul McCartney recalled meeting her in Nashville and expressed the honor of having her sing his song "Let It Be," praising her songwriting and singing.
caption:
The queen of country music is gone. Dolly Parton has died at 80 after a private battle with cancer.

Legendary country singer and actress Dolly Parton has passed away at the age of 80. According to a statement from her family, she died on August 25 after privately battling cancer.

Parton is globally recognized for her timeless hits such as "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You," as well as her significant contributions to film and philanthropy.

Music and Hollywood stars have poured out their tributes. Reba McEntire praised Parton's "huge heart," while Lily Tomlin called her the "Great Harmonizer of Humanity."

Taylor Swift described the icon as a "gift that kept on giving," noting her influence on young women and her "backbone of steel" as an artist.

US President Donald Trump mourned the loss, calling her one of the greatest country singers and describing her death as a "true loss for millions of people."

Other tributes came from Jane Fonda, Sally Field, and Julia Roberts, who remembered her kindness, humor, and magical spirit.

Paul McCartney recalled meeting her in Nashville and expressed the honor of having her sing his song "Let It Be," praising her songwriting and singing.
